title: [Audit] 🗂️ Kibana Object Forensics
description: Every Kibana saved-object read and change, by type, name, space and actor.

config.description: All Kibana audit events. Usually a small fraction of raw stream volume, but most of the forensic value — this is where saved objects, spaces and sessions are recorded.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" | STATS `Kibana events` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Every Kibana state change in range, selected by ECS event.type rather than by an action-name suffix. That matters: a suffix test cannot see rule_enable, rule_disable, the whole case_user_action family, or anything the workflow, ML and agent-builder features emit, because none of those action names end in _create/_update/_delete. Point-in-time open/close are ECS-tagged creation/deletion but are query internals, and are excluded by name.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | STATS `Mutations` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Distinct Kibana objects accessed or modified in range — reads included, as the name says. Identity is attributes.kibana.saved_object.id where Kibana records one and is recovered from body.text otherwise, because workflows, ML jobs and agent-builder tools carry no saved_object fields at all.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" | GROK body.text """\[(?:id|workflowId)=%{DATA:g_id}(?:,|\])""" | EVAL obj_id = COALESCE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.id, g_id) | STATS `Objects touched` = COUNT_DISTINCT(obj_id)

config.description: How many different kinds of thing were involved (dashboard, alert, index-pattern, tag, workflow …). Restricted to events that actually name an object: without that guard the derived type falls back to the action name and http_request — logged for every Kibana request — would count as an object type.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" | GROK body.text """\[(?:id|workflowId)=%{DATA:g_id}(?:,|\])""" | EVAL obj_id = COALESCE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.id, g_id) | WHERE obj_id IS NOT NULL | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY attributes.event.action, attributes.kibana.saved_object.type | EVAL obj_type = CASE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL, attributes.kibana.saved_object.type, attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_job", "ml-job", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_datafeed", "ml-datafeed", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_execution_*", "workflow-execution", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_*", "workflow", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_agent_*", "agent-builder-agent", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_tool_*", "agent-builder-tool", attributes.event.action LIKE "product_documentation_*", "product-documentation", attributes.event.action == "secret_create", "secret", attributes.event.action IS NULL, "unclassified", REPLACE(attributes.event.action, "_(create|update|delete|enable|disable|run|run_soon|test|cancel)$", "")) | STATS `Object types` = COUNT_DISTINCT(obj_type)

config.description: Distinct identities that changed anything in Kibana in range, resolved the same way every other actor panel resolves them. Counting emails alone misses changes made by credentials that carry no email. Includes people who only enabled a rule, ran a workflow or created an ML job — none of which an action-name suffix test counts as a change.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS `Editors` = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor)

config.title: ⚠️ Mutations — most recent Kibana state changes, repeats grouped into one row · 30 at most
config.description: The single most important panel in the suite: state changes in Kibana, with who did it, what it was called, and which space it lives in. Each row groups the same change made again: one identity, one operation, one object, one space and one result over the whole time range. Events is how many times that happened and Last change is the newest of them, so a row reading Events 17 is seventeen changes, and the Mutations tile counts each one. The table holds the 30 groups changed most recently; every change in range is in "All mutations" on Security & Anomalies, and the "Kibana saved-object activity" session further down this page lists reads and changes together. Two columns to read carefully. Object type and Object are the real saved-object fields where Kibana records them and are otherwise recovered from the event message, because workflows, ML jobs and agent-builder objects carry no saved_object fields. A workflow cancel, or a test of an unsaved draft, names only its run, so it reads "execution" and the run id's first 8 characters. Result is "attempted" where Kibana logged the attempt rather than the outcome — that is how the saved-object path records things, so it is normal, and a "failure" here is a change that was denied. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. The table holds more rows than the panel shows: scroll it for the rest.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | GROK body.text """\[(?:id|workflowId)=%{DATA:g_id}(?:,|\])""" | GROK body.text """\[name=%{GREEDYDATA:g_name}\]""" | GROK body.text """\[executionId=%{DATA:g_exec}\]""" | GROK body.text """case id: %{NOTSPACE:g_case}""" | GROK body.text """(?:job|datafeed) %{NOTSPACE:g_ml}""" | EVAL obj_name = COALESCE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.name, g_name, g_id, attributes.kibana.saved_object.id, g_case, g_ml, g_exec, body.text) | EVAL result = CASE(attributes.event.outcome == "unknown", "attempted", attributes.event.outcome) | EVAL execution = COALESCE(LEFT(g_exec, 8), "—") | EVAL is_exec = obj_name == g_exec | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS n = COUNT(*), last_ts = MAX(@timestamp) BY actor, attributes.event.action, attributes.kibana.saved_object.type, obj_name, space = attributes.kibana.space.id, result, is_exec | EVAL verb = CASE(attributes.event.action LIKE "*_execution_cancel", "cancel", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run_soon", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_test", "test", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_enable", "enable", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_disable", "disable", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_put_*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_open_*", "open", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_start_*", "start", attributes.event.action LIKE "*point_in_time", "pit", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_create*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_update*", "update", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_delete", "delete", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_find", "find", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_get", "get", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_resolve", "resolve", "other") | EVAL obj_type = CASE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL, attributes.kibana.saved_object.type, attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_job", "ml-job", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_datafeed", "ml-datafeed", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_execution_*", "workflow-execution", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_*", "workflow", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_agent_*", "agent-builder-agent", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_tool_*", "agent-builder-tool", attributes.event.action LIKE "product_documentation_*", "product-documentation", attributes.event.action == "secret_create", "secret", attributes.event.action IS NULL, "unclassified", REPLACE(attributes.event.action, "_(create|update|delete|enable|disable|run|run_soon|test|cancel)$", "")) | STATS events = SUM(n), last_change = MAX(last_ts) BY actor, verb, type = obj_type, name = obj_name, space, result, is_exec | SORT last_change DESC | LIMIT 30 | EVAL name = CASE(is_exec, CONCAT("execution ", LEFT(name, 8)), name) | EVAL actor = CASE((LENGTH(actor) == 20 AND actor RLIKE "[-_A-Za-z0-9]{20}" AND NOT actor RLIKE "[0-9]{20}"), CONCAT(LEFT(actor, 5), "… · Cloud API key"), actor)

config.title: Object type × operation
config.description: Saved-object type against operation, writes first; all Kibana traffic, reads included. Cell colour is the event count on a log scale, running teal (fewest) through blue and purple to pink (most); the legend spans exactly the counts drawn. Every cell has an outline, so a single create, update or delete stays visible beside thousands of reads: the write columns are the forensic signal. Past 13 object types the rest share one "N more types" row at the bottom; types with any write rank first, so a rare change is never the one folded away. Hover a cell for its count and how many distinct objects it covers.

config.title: Kibana state changes over time · reads in the heatmap
config.description: The Mutations tile over time, by operation: the same events, so the bars add up to that tile. Creates, updates and deletes each have a colour; every other change — enabling, disabling, running, testing or cancelling a rule or workflow, opening or starting an ML job, removing references — is one "other change" series, because each is a few events a day and would be a sliver no one could see. The Mutations table above names each one. Reads are left out because they outnumber changes about thirty to one and flattened every change into a sliver; the heatmap beside this panel and the Object types table below show them. A deploy shows as a block of creates, updates and deletes together.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | STATS n = COUNT(*) BY BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), attributes.event.action | EVAL verb = CASE(attributes.event.action LIKE "*_execution_cancel", "cancel", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run_soon", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_test", "test", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_enable", "enable", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_disable", "disable", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_put_*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_open_*", "open", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_start_*", "start", attributes.event.action LIKE "*point_in_time", "pit", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_create*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_update*", "update", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_delete", "delete", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_find", "find", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_get", "get", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_resolve", "resolve", "other") | EVAL verb = CASE(verb IN ("create", "update", "delete"), verb, "other change") | STATS events = SUM(n) BY `BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend)`, verb | SORT verb != "create", verb != "update", verb != "delete"

config.title: Busiest objects · suite left out · top 10 at most (empty when none outside the suite)
config.description: Object titles from kibana.saved_object.name, or the object's id where Kibana recorded no title (a space, or the advanced-settings object, whose id is the Kibana version such as 9.6.0), ranked by events, reads and changes together. Like the high-value table beside it, this leaves out what the noise gate calls query internals: views of this audit suite's own dashboards, searches and data view, the suite's automated install (the API imports, exports and writes that deploy it, with no browser session), and the settings and data-view lookups every Kibana page load makes, which otherwise filled every row with the suite watching and installing itself. So when nothing outside the suite was opened or changed in range the table is empty, while the tiles above still count those views. A suite object a person changed in Kibana is kept; every change, the install's included, is in Mutations above. Identities counts people and API keys alike, resolved the way every actor panel resolves them. The tiles, the heatmap and the Object types table still count suite views: they read all Kibana traffic. On a narrow screen a long object name wraps onto a second line. This panel is empty when none outside the suite. The table holds more rows than the panel shows: scroll it for the rest.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.kibana.saved_object.id IS NOT NULL | WHERE attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time","space_get","space_find") OR (attributes.event.action == "http_request" AND attributes.url.original IS NOT NULL AND attributes.url.original RLIKE "https?://[^/]+(/s/[^/]+)?/((internal|translations|app)/.*|api/content_management/rpc/(get|search|mget|bulkGet).*|bootstrap(-anonymous)?[.]js.*|api/(core|licensing|banners|ui_counters)/.*|api/spaces/space([?].*)?)|https?://[^/]+(/s/[^/]+)?/api/(saved_objects/(_import|_export)|[^?]*/(elastic_)?cloud-audit-).*") OR (attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL AND ((attributes.event.action == "saved_object_get" AND attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IN ("config","config-global")) OR (attributes.event.action == "saved_object_find" AND attributes.kibana.saved_object.type == "index-pattern"))) OR (attributes.kibana.saved_object.id IS NOT NULL AND (attributes.kibana.saved_object.id LIKE "cloud-audit-*" OR attributes.kibana.saved_object.id LIKE "elastic_cloud-audit-*") AND (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_get","saved_object_resolve","saved_object_find") OR attributes.kibana.session.id IS NULL))) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS events = COUNT(*), actors = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor) BY name = COALESCE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.name, attributes.kibana.saved_object.id), type = attributes.kibana.saved_object.type | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Latest high-value object access · suite left out · 10 at most (empty when none outside the suite)
config.description: The ten most recent reads and changes of the high-value object types: dashboards, data views, SLOs, alert rules, tags, workflows, agent-builder agents and tools, and ML jobs — who touched which one, and when. A type that nobody touched in range has no rows. Unlike the panel beside it, this one leaves out what the noise gate calls query internals: views of this audit suite's own dashboards and data view and its automated install (API imports, exports and writes with no browser session), page-load lookups, space lookups and point-in-time paging, which on a deployed suite would fill every row. So when no high-value object outside the suite was opened or changed in range the table is empty. A suite object a person changed in Kibana is kept; every change, the install's included, is in Mutations above. Both `alert` and `alerting_rule` are included, because Kibana records the same rule under either type depending on which code path audited it. On a narrow screen a long object name wraps onto a second line. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. This panel is empty when none outside the suite. The table holds more rows than the panel shows: scroll it for the rest.

config.title: Object types · suite included · up to 9
config.description: All Kibana traffic, the suite's own included, unlike the two tables above: the saved-object types with the most events, busiest first, reads and changes, as in the heatmap above (which splits each type by operation). Objects is how many distinct objects of that type were touched. "space" ranks high because every Kibana page load reads the active space. The space row's Objects can run above the Spaces tile: the tile counts spaces something happened in, and a space that was only created, or created and deleted, with nothing done inside it (or a create that was denied) is a space object touched but not a space with activity.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*), objects = COUNT_DISTINCT(attributes.kibana.saved_object.id) BY type = attributes.kibana.saved_object.type | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 9

config.title: Busiest spaces by id · all traffic · up to 10
config.description: Kibana activity in the ten busiest spaces, all Kibana traffic like the Spaces tile; hover a bar for its count. A space is shown by its id, the /s/<id> in its URL: the audit stream records no space display name, not even on a space read. Spaces that tooling creates and deletes (review or test spaces) are real activity and rank like any other. Viewing these audit dashboards counts too: each panel load is audited in the space it is viewed from, so the space the suite is installed in, and any space it is rendered in for review, carries its own reads.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.kibana.space.id IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY space = attributes.kibana.space.id | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Cross-space activity · all traffic
config.description: Identities ranked by how many Kibana spaces they touched; Spaces is the count, and Space list names them alphabetically on up to three lines — a longer list ends in "…", and the ⤢ at a row's left opens the whole list. Anything above one space is worth understanding. All Kibana traffic, like the Spaces tile. Events counts events recorded in a space, so the column can add up to slightly less than the Kibana events tile: a sign-in (user_login) belongs to no space. A space is shown by its id, the /s/<id> in its URL: the audit stream records no space display name, not even on a space read. Spaces that tooling creates and deletes (review or test spaces) are real activity and rank like any other. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.

config.title: Kibana saved-object activity · suite left out · newest 1,000 at most
config.description: Kibana events that named an object, reads and changes, newest first; the newest 1,000 in range, so the result count above the grid is that cap, not a total. Like the two tables above, it leaves out what the noise gate calls query internals (views of this audit suite's own dashboards, searches and data view, its automated install, page-load lookups, space lookups and point-in-time paging), which otherwise filled every visible row with the suite watching and installing itself. A suite object a person changed in Kibana is kept; every change, the install's included, is in Mutations at the top of the page. Kibana's page requests and logins name no object and are left out too. Object is the title the object had when the event was recorded, so a renamed object shows its old title on older rows; the id in Message does not change. Open in Discover to filter on a column or page further back. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email.

config.title: Session reconstruction · newest 1,000 at most (empty when no browser session opened or changed anything)
config.description: One person's Kibana sessions, event by event, newest first: every object they opened and changed, with the sentence Kibana wrote for each, which names the object's type and id ("User has resolved dashboard [id=…]"). Operation uses the same words as the heatmap (get, resolve, create …); an event that names no object keeps its own action, such as "http request" for a public API call. Pin an identity first, then open in Discover, filter to one Session and sort Time ascending to replay it forward. Kibana's internal UI requests, usage counters, space lookups and point-in-time internals are left out; public API calls such as an export are kept, and so are views of this audit suite, because they are part of what the person did. That is why the panel can be empty while Cross-space activity above counts a signed-in person: a browser tab left open keeps sending those background requests (tag lists, usage counters, paging) without the person opening or changing anything. Object is the title the object had at the time, so a renamed object shows its old title on older rows. Session is printed in full, so it can be read and copied; on a narrow screen the grid scrolls sideways for Space and Message. API-key traffic carries no session. An Identity shown as “_4KEO… · Cloud API key” is an organization-level Elastic Cloud API key: the audit stream records it only by its opaque 20-character id, shown here by its first five characters; it has no name and no owner email. This panel is empty when no browser session opened or changed anything.
